On phones narrower than about 370 px the row can still wrap, and no test covers that. - **Rail width.** The desktop rail is 208 px (186 px inside). A worded per-row button wraps every row's count and chip (measured), so the row gets the 28 px icon. Even so, a row whose chip is long (such as "3 not owned") can wrap its meta line, as "Practice only" already does. - **e2e selectors.** The specs pick rows with `[data-testid^="deck-row-"]`. The new id must not start with `deck-row-`. - **Ownership refusals.** The server refuses a portrait or pick the account does not own (R1827000, R1833000). A copy of a deck holding such a legacy pick is refused like any save of the original would be, and the refusal shows on the copy (R256). Nothing to build. - **Hidden information and determinism.** Neither is affected: client only, nothing enters `view_for`, the engine or a replay. Rule 7 holds because the server still enforces the cap (`decks_upsert`), and the client only disables the button early. **Open questions.** These are decisions I made that the task did not settle; a person may overrule any of them. - **No ruling.** Duplicate is a deck-workshop convenience over the existing upsert and caps (R250, R252, R256), like #2007's "Practice with this deck", which added none. Rejected: a note R2096000 plus an §9.4 line. - **Literal names.** Duplicating "Aggro (copy)" gives "Aggro (copy) (copy)", following the issue's ` (copy)` exactly. Rejected: stripping a trailing "(copy n)" first, which would mean parsing a localised suffix. - **The name is cut to fit.** The original's name is shortened so the suffix survives the 40-character cap. Rejected: letting the save's cut drop " (copy)", which would repeat the original's name. - **List action shape.** A per-row icon button whose accessible name and tooltip are "Duplicate {deck}". Rejected: a worded per-row button (wraps the narrow rail) and a group-head button acting on the open deck (on a phone it is unclear which deck it copies). - **Editor reason.** The editor states its own reason at the cap, because a phone's editor half hides the rail's note. - **Save timing.** The copy saves through the usual debounce, not at once. ````
